days.title: 'It's not editable' turned out to be three different bugs
days.angle: build receipt — a real fix, measured against hand-computed truth
days.proof_plan: A designer reported fixtures could not be moved on the plan canvas. It resolved into two unrelated causes, neither obvious: a canvas layer built with listening disabled, so the hit graph was dead; and a calibration anchored to the four corners of the image, assuming the plan bleeds edge to edge. px/ft X 47.82 -> 40.31 against a hand-computed truth of 40.30. px/ft Y 41.96 -> 40.39 (truth 40.39). Anisotropy 1.1396 -> 0.998 (truth 1.000). Fixtures had been drawn 18.6% too wide and up to ~1.7 ft out of place; one chair box sat outside the building. Test suite 859 -> 871 green.
days.method_layer: Durable lesson for both audiences: auto-derived config must announce itself. The calibration was wrong for months because a plausible number displayed with no provenance. Include that the falsifier fired in the same session — aspect-only outline detection picked an interior rectangle on another plan. A fallback indistinguishable from a real answer is a bug, not a fallback.
days.notes: SWAPPED 2026-09-20, replacing idea-020. idea-020's central fact (the model supplying the wrong country's state emblem) cannot be published under the naming clearance on record — it would reveal the chamber's emblem/portrait arrangement. idea-019 carries comparable engineering weight, has hard before/after numbers against hand-computed truth, and has ZERO client exposure: it is about our own canvas tool, not the client's room. Reframe the hook around the measured fix (px/ft 47.82 -> 40.31 against truth 40.30), not around the word 'editable'.
